groups.label: Body, Soul, and Medical Care
groups.summary: These commentaries examine the relationship between physical and mental well-being, exploring the harmonization of spirited and rational faculties through music and gymnastics while critiquing Plato's views on bodily medicine and gradual healing.
groups.rationale: Both entries address the interaction of mind and body, gymnastics, and the proper management of bodily health and soul harmony.

groups.label: Civic Good and Priority of Duty
groups.summary: This selection discusses state governance, arguing that political order aims at the happiness and excellence of the whole commonwealth rather than any single faction, with moral duty and fundamental education taking precedence over piecemeal statutes.
groups.rationale: All three entries address the primary objectives of the state, contrasting foundational moral duty and educational character-building with utilitarian happiness and petty legal codes.

groups.label: Harmonic Order in Soul and State
groups.summary: These passages define justice and civic unity across the tripartite soul and the state, describing how functional division of labor and mutual harmony enable both the individual psyche and the polis to operate as integrated organisms.
groups.rationale: These entries center on the structural correspondence between the three principles of the soul and the unified classes of the just commonwealth.

groups.label: Philosopher-Rulers and Society
groups.summary: Socrates proposes that just governance requires uniting political rule with philosophy, while also warning of the acute vulnerability of noble philosophic characters to corruption by public pressure and popular opinion.
groups.rationale: Both nodes focus on the role of the philosopher in politics, the conditions required for philosophic rule, and the social obstacles facing philosophic natures.

groups.label: Epistemology and the Good
groups.summary: This sequence articulates Plato's central metaphysical and epistemological doctrines, distinguishing knowledge from opinion and employing the analogies of the Sun, the Divided Line, and the Cave to chart the soul's ascent toward the supreme Idea of the Good.
groups.rationale: A contiguous set of passages from Books V–VII outlining Plato's core epistemological ladder and the metaphysical status of the Good.

groups.label: Lifelong Education and Ideals
groups.summary: These later overview sections examine the broader significance of Platonic philosophy, highlighting education as a lifelong redirection of the soul toward the light and considering how transcendent ideals—including the Idea of the Good and the concept of the Divine Man—elevate human conduct.
groups.rationale: These nodes from the concluding essays evaluate the enduring significance of Platonic ideals and life-encompassing education.
